messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT P1] runtime-serving latency spike detected on canary pool 'slice-c' — p95 jumped 120ms -> 980ms, error rate 3.2%, alert id A-3051
Priya: paging SREs for immediate triage, I'm taking the lead. @Ethan @Maya please ack
Ethan: ack, pulling canary dashboards and node metrics now
Maya: seeing continuous batching throughput collapse and kernel fallbacks rising on nodes hosting slice-c
Ethan: stack traces show kernel selection falling back to slow quant kernel frequently; batching aggregator mis-sized in a few traces
Priya: deploy-bot shows a deploy ~10m ago (ts 3051233500) that included runtime v2.3.4 + new batching heuristic/thresholds. Could be related
Liam: can we flip the feature flag `batch-heuristic-v2` off for canary as a quick kill-switch?
Ethan: agreed — that should short-circuit the new path. Priya, can you toggle?
Priya: running: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"batch-heuristic-v2","scope":"canary","value":false}'`
deploy-bot: flag update accepted for scope=canary, flag=batch-heuristic-v2 -> false
Maya: metrics 60s after flag flip: p95 dropped to ~420ms (was 980), qps recovering but still 30% below baseline
Ethan: kernel fallback rate decreased but not back to baseline; looks like some nodes still haven't fully drained bad state (KV cache misses high)
Priya: if recovery stalls in 10m we should rollback the runtime image on the canary set. @Liam, do you want to lead the rollback?
Liam: yes — target a targeted canary revert to v2.3.3 (no batching heuristic change). Starting canary rollback on the 12 machines identified
deploy-bot: initiating rollback job: revert image -> runtime:v2.3.3 on 12 hosts (slice-c). ETA ~3m per host staggered
Ethan: attaching quick trace snippet where fallback triggered: `kernel_select.go: line 214` decision path hit because `aggregator.size=0` in a few cases — likely an off-by-one in threshold logic introduced in 2.3.4
Maya: uploaded heapdump+traces to artifacts: /var/logs/trace/3051234567/traces.tgz for postmortem
Priya: customer-impact update: Support reported 2 paying customers on canary-exposed routes experiencing high tail latency; CS notified and monitoring for escalations. No 5xx user-facing errors reported so far
Liam: posting to #customer-impact with recommended mitigation: temporarily route affected customers to stable route/model and offer timeout guidance to clients
ops-runbook-bot: Handoff note — if not resolved in 45m hand off to on-call rotation @Liam. Runbook excerpt: if p95 > 500ms after rollback, perform traffic-shift to stable pool or scale dedicated pool; open incident follow-up ticket
Ethan: rollback completed on all 12 canary nodes — checks passing. canary p95 now ~110ms, qps restored to expected levels
Maya: kernel fallback and aggregator error counts back to baseline. No further evidence of persistent KV eviction loops
Priya: great work. Closing the active pager for A-3051. Opening follow-up issue: `runtime#4732` to add regression test and tighten aggregator invariants, and capture postmortem notes + RCA
Liam: leaving a short note for release team: revert accepted, don't reintroduce `batch-heuristic-v2` until test coverage and synthetic workload validation are in place :thumbsup:
Priya: handing over monitoring to next on-call, I'll remain available for the postmortem. Thanks everyone for quick action
IncidentBot: Pager resolved: A-3051 closed by Priya at ts 3051234599
